name: huginndb
description: Let an AI client inspect and query the databases HuginnDB already knows about — PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB and SQL Server — with a per-connection write policy.
long_description:
HuginnDB's headless MCP connector exposes the connections saved in the HuginnDB desktop app, reading their passwords from the OS keychain. An assistant can inspect real schema, browse rows, run read-only statements, read server health and — only where you allow it — write.

Requires the HuginnDB desktop app on the same machine: this extension reads its saved connection profiles and their keychain entries. Which connections it may reach is chosen in the app under Settings → MCP, and re-read on every call, so nothing is reachable until you tick it and no client restart is needed after you do.

Everything stays on your machine. The connector opens database connections directly from this computer; it has no server, no account and no telemetry.

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: Which databases this server is allowed to reach.

tools.name: list_databases
tools.description: Databases / schemas / catalogs on a connection.

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: Tables and views, with approximate row counts and sizes.

tools.name: describe_table
tools.description: Columns, types, nullability, primary key, foreign keys and indexes.

tools.name: list_indexes
tools.description: Indexes on a table and the columns each covers.

tools.name: run_query
tools.description: Run a single read-only statement and return its rows.

tools.name: run_write
tools.description: Run a single statement that changes the database, where the connection's write policy allows it.

tools.name: run_queries
tools.description: Run several read-only statements in one call.

tools.name: run_writes
tools.description: Apply several row writes in one transaction, with optional reads to verify them after the commit.

tools.name: run_script
tools.description: Run a whole SQL script (inline or a local .sql file) on one session, so temporary tables and SETs carry across statements; one transaction by default.

tools.name: browse_table
tools.description: Browse one page of rows without writing SQL.

tools.name: server_version
tools.description: The connected engine and version.

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: Server-side users and roles.

tools.name: list_privileges
tools.description: The privileges granted to a user or role.

tools.name: pulse_health
tools.description: Live vital signs: queries/s, connection pressure, cache hit rate.

tools.name: pulse_metrics
tools.description: One metric's stored history from the on-disk sampler.

tools.name: pulse_top_queries
tools.description: Statements the server has spent the most time on.

tools.name: pulse_explain
tools.description: The plan the server would use for one statement, without running it.

tools.name: pulse_storage
tools.description: The biggest relations, split into data, index and free space.

tools.name: pulse_sessions
tools.description: Sessions or operations currently open on the server.

tools.name: pulse_index_usage
tools.description: Index usage across the biggest relations, least-read first.

tools.name: insert_row
tools.description: Insert one row. Needs the 'data' write policy.

tools.name: update_cell
tools.description: Update one column of the row addressed by its full primary key. Needs 'data'.

tools.name: delete_rows
tools.description: Delete rows addressed by their full primary keys. Needs 'data'.

tools.name: save_view
tools.description: Create, redefine or rename a view. Needs the 'full' write policy.

tools.name: drop_view
tools.description: Drop a view. Needs 'full'.

tools.name: create_index
tools.description: MongoDB only. Create one index. Needs 'full'.

tools.name: drop_index
tools.description: MongoDB only. Drop one index by name. Needs 'full'.
